concerns.text: FR-008 mandates a sensitivity analysis sweeping variance thresholds including '[deferred]' (e.g., '90%, 95%, [deferred]'). This contradicts the spec's own definition of '[deferred]' in the 'Sanctioned [deferred] markers' section of the review protocol, which states planning docs must name the metric and reference, not use the marker as a placeholder value in a list of concrete thresholds. A requirement cannot mandate testing a non-existent threshold labeled '[deferred]'.

Acceptance Scenario 1 requires the system to select 'the minimum number required to explain ≥95% of cumulative variance'. However, FR-008 requires a sensitivity analysis sweeping '90%, 95%, [deferred]'. If the system must sweep 90% and 99% (implied by 'high-confidence levels'), the 'minimum number' for 95% is not the only output; the requirement implies a single fixed target (95%) while the FR implies a range. The acceptance criteria must be broadened to reflect the sensitivity analysis or the FR must be narrowed to a single fixed threshold to avoid contradiction.

Acceptance Scenario 3 defines a 'plateau' as '<0.001 change in loss over 5 consecutive epochs'. However, the training duration in User Story 1 and the methodology is explicitly '3 epochs'. It is mathematically impossible to observe a plateau over '5 consecutive epochs' if the total training duration is only 3 epochs. This creates a logical contradiction where the acceptance criteria can never be met.
